final_proof:
Let \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\in\mathbb N_0^n\). For a tuple \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\) and a multiindex \(\gamma\), recall that
\[
z^\gamma=\prod_{j=1}^n z_j^{\gamma_j},\qquad \binom{\alpha}{\gamma}=\prod_{j=1}^n\binom{\alpha_j}{\gamma_j},
\]
and that \(0\leq\gamma\leq\alpha\) means \(0\leq\gamma_j\leq\alpha_j\) for every \(j\).

By the ordinary binomial theorem, for each \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\),
\[
(x_j+y_j)^{\alpha_j}=\sum_{b_j=0}^{\alpha_j}\binom{\alpha_j}{b_j}x_j^{b_j}y_j^{\alpha_j-b_j}.
\]
Using the definition of a multiindex power and multiplying these \(n\) finite sums, the distributive law gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x+y)^\alpha
&=\prod_{j=1}^n(x_j+y_j)^{\alpha_j}\\
&=\prod_{j=1}^n\left(\sum_{b_j=0}^{\alpha_j}\binom{\alpha_j}{b_j}x_j^{b_j}y_j^{\alpha_j-b_j}\right)\\
&=\sum_{b_1=0}^{\alpha_1}\cdots\sum_{b_n=0}^{\alpha_n}\prod_{j=1}^n\left(\binom{\alpha_j}{b_j}x_j^{b_j}y_j^{\alpha_j-b_j}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The tuples \(\beta=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)\) occurring in this iterated sum are precisely the multiindices satisfying \(0\leq\beta\leq\alpha\). Moreover, for every such \(\beta\),
\[
\prod_{j=1}^n\left(\binom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j}x_j^{\beta_j}y_j^{\alpha_j-\beta_j}\right)=\left(\prod_{j=1}^n\binom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j}\right)\left(\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{\beta_j}\right)\left(\prod_{j=1}^n y_j^{\alpha_j-\beta_j}\right)=\binom{\alpha}{\beta}x^\beta y^{\alpha-\beta}.
\]
Substitution into the preceding finite sum therefore yields
\[
(x+y)^\alpha=\sum_{0\leq\beta\leq\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}x^\beta y^{\alpha-\beta},
\]
as required.
